mnemolith.configuration.title: Mnemolith
mnemolith.configuration.recollectionStor: Multiplier on the saturated, overloaded, and fracture thresholds. Each scaled threshold is capped at pressureSoftCap, so fracture stays reachable. Recollection storms can only gather in a fractured chunk, so this also sets how loud a place must get before a storm is possible: higher means later and rarer storms.
Soft cap for memory pressure accumulated from imprints in loaded chunks.
mnemolith.configuration.imprintNodeWeigh: Reserved, not used yet: no worldgen feature places imprint-bearing nodes. Relative weight of such nodes when structures are placed.
mnemolith.configuration.stormAttemptChan: Chance, from 0.0 to 1.0, rolled once a second for each player standing in a fractured chunk, that a recollection storm starts gathering there (if allowRecollectionStorms, maxStormsPerDimension, mute stones and scar wards allow it). 0.02 means a storm usually gathers within a minute or two. 0 turns natural storms off; a freed residual shard can still call one.
mnemolith.configuration.structuresEnable: Whether the chronicle observatory may generate. Applies the next time a world loads.
mnemolith.configuration.structureSpacing: Documented observatory spacing in chunks. The structure set uses 32, with 12 chunks of separation.
mnemolith.configuration.archivalVeinsEna: Whether archival veins generate in the overworld.
mnemolith.configuration.archivalVeinChan: Chance, out of 100, that a chunk attempts an archival vein.
mnemolith.configuration.archivalVeinMinY: Lowest Y of an archival vein.
mnemolith.configuration.archivalVeinMaxY: Highest Y of an archival vein.
mnemolith.configuration.archivalVeinSize: Length, in blocks, of one archival vein.
mnemolith.configuration.archivalBleed.to: Pressure added per archival stratum block.
mnemolith.configuration.archivalBleedCap: Most stratum blocks that add pressure in one chunk.
mnemolith.configuration.mutePocketsEnabl: Whether mute pockets generate. Their mute stone blocks writes.
mnemolith.configuration.mutePocketChance: Chance, out of 100, that a chunk attempts a mute pocket.
mnemolith.configuration.mutePocketMinY.t: Lowest Y of a mute pocket.
mnemolith.configuration.mutePocketMaxY.t: Highest Y of a mute pocket.
mnemolith.configuration.observatoryEnabl: Whether chronicle observatories generate. Also requires structures enabled.
mnemolith.configuration.archivistObserva: Lowers an archivist's pressure gate near an observatory.
Lowers an echo strider's pressure gate in a chunk that holds a path imprint.
mnemolith.configuration.compositionEnabl: Whether players may compose extracted imprints.
mnemolith.configuration.maxImprintsPerCh: Maximum imprints stored on a single chunk.
mnemolith.configuration.allowRecollectio: Whether recollection storms may gather, naturally or called by a freed residual shard. Turning it off ends storms that are running (their residues stay as ordinary residues); Scar sites and the Scar stay.
mnemolith.configuration.maxStormsPerDime: Maximum recollection storms gathering or raging in one dimension at once. 0 stops new storms like allowRecollectionStorms false, without ending running ones.
mnemolith.configuration.logPressureChang: Whether pressure changes are written to the server log.
mnemolith.configuration.imprintParticles: Whether custom memory particles are shown.
mnemolith.configuration.pressureVignette: Whether an overloaded or fractured chunk darkens the screen edge. The band comes from the server.
mnemolith.configuration.stormScreenShake: Whether an overloaded or fractured chunk (where recollection storms gather) shakes the camera. Client only: it never starts or stops a storm, and the storm's darkened sky and fog come with its boss bar either way.
mnemolith.configuration.fractureFringe.t: Whether the fractured chunk under you desaturates the world and fringes the screen edge. Overloaded chunks do not.
mnemolith.configuration.memoryAudioVolum: Volume scale, from 0.0 to 1.0, for the local chronicle lens chime.
Scale, from 0.0 to 1.0, for every custom memory particle. 0 disables them.
mnemolith.configuration.maxParticlesPerT: Hard cap on custom memory particles spawned in one client tick. Density still scales the budget, and 0 density disables them.
mnemolith.configuration.ambientWithoutLe: Whether saturated chunks shimmer when the chronicle lens is not held. Vein marks stay lens-only.
mnemolith.configuration.lensPollInterval: Ticks between chronicle lens pressure requests.
mnemolith.configuration.writeDebounceTic: Ticks that must pass before another build or redstone imprint can be written in the same chunk.
mnemolith.configuration.writeDeath.toolt: Whether a death writes a death imprint.
mnemolith.configuration.writeExplosion.t: Whether an explosion writes an explosion imprint.
mnemolith.configuration.writeFall.toolti: Whether a significant fall writes a fall imprint.
mnemolith.configuration.writeBuild.toolt: Whether placing or breaking a block writes a build or redstone imprint.
Minimum fall distance, in blocks, before a fall imprint is written.
mnemolith.configuration.extractionDurabi: Durability the extraction needle loses on a successful extract.
mnemolith.configuration.extractionCooldo: Ticks before the extraction needle can extract again. 0 disables the cooldown.
mnemolith.configuration.failurePressureS: Instability added to the composition reel's chunk when a formula fails. A replicant is asked only if that chunk is then overloaded or fractured.
mnemolith.configuration.instabilityDecay: Instability removed from a player's chunk on each decay pulse. 0 disables cooling.
Ticks between instability and quiet-imprint pulses while a player is in the chunk. 0 disables the pulse.
mnemolith.configuration.allowAmbientPres: Whether the server sends full nearby pressure snapshots to a player who is not holding a chronicle lens. Without it, fracture feel still works from overloaded and fracture bands only. Vein marks stay lens-only. The client Ambient Without Lens toggle only draws that shimmer.
mnemolith.configuration.veinShimmerTicks: Ticks between vein particle repeats while a held lens snapshot has not changed. 0 repeats only when the snapshot is new. A changed chunk still shimmers immediately.
mnemolith.configuration.quietFadeTicks.t: Ticks before the oldest build, redstone, or path imprint can fade. Loud imprints stay until extracted. 0 disables the fade.
mnemolith.configuration.saturatedThresho: Pressure at which a chunk becomes saturated. Multiplied by the storm threshold and capped at the soft cap.
mnemolith.configuration.overloadedThresh: Pressure at which a chunk becomes overloaded. Multiplied by the storm threshold and capped at the soft cap.
mnemolith.configuration.fractureThreshol: Pressure at which a chunk fractures. Multiplied by the storm threshold and capped at the soft cap. Fracture is logged, can spawn a moment replicant, and is where a recollection storm can gather.
mnemolith.configuration.muteRadiusChunks: Chebyshev radius, in chunks, where a mute stone blocks imprint writes. 0 is the stone's own chunk.
mnemolith.configuration.echoStriderEnabl: Whether echo striders may spawn from pressure and whether their AI runs.
mnemolith.configuration.archivistEnabled: Whether archivists may spawn from pressure and whether they steal slips.
mnemolith.configuration.momentReplicantE: Whether moment replicants may spawn from fracture, an overloaded composition failure, or natural pressure.
mnemolith.configuration.echoStriderDamag: Attack damage of an echo strider charge.
Attack damage when a moment replicant copies a melee hit.
mnemolith.configuration.archivistStealCo: Ticks an archivist waits after a theft before it can steal again.
mnemolith.configuration.echoStriderSpawn: Chance, out of 100, that a natural echo strider spawn attempt is kept.
mnemolith.configuration.archivistSpawnWe: Chance, out of 100, that a natural archivist spawn attempt is kept.
mnemolith.configuration.replicantSpawnWe: Chance, out of 100, that a natural moment replicant spawn attempt is kept.
mnemolith.configuration.echoStriderMinPr: Minimum cached pressure before an echo strider can spawn naturally.
mnemolith.configuration.archivistMinPres: Minimum cached pressure before an archivist can spawn naturally. The default sits on the overloaded band.
mnemolith.configuration.replicantMinPres: Minimum cached pressure before a moment replicant can spawn naturally.
mnemolith.configuration.sensorInterval.t: Ticks between archivist resonator scans, flee pressure scans, and idle strider repaths. A charge still aims every tick. 1 checks every tick.
item.mnemolith.chronicle_lens.hint: Hold to read memory pressure as a pill above the hotbar. Sneak for the chunk state. Near archival strata the read reaches one chunk farther, and the stone glows. Sneak and use to blind moment replicants.
item.mnemolith.extraction_needle.hint: Use on a block to pull the strongest imprint into a slip. It rests for a moment between pulls. In a stratum chunk, an empty read also checks the neighbor chunks. Use on your own echo to unpick its graft.
mnemolith.message.extract_empty: This chunk has no imprint to extract.
mnemolith.message.compose_fail: The slips refuse to hold together.
mnemolith.command.perf: Perf pathNs %s buildNs %s scoreNs %s syncNs %s skipped %s sensorNs %s
mnemolith.command.mpsmoke: MP smoke sameBand %s discovery %s steal %s reel %s mute %s replicants %s guarded %s
item.mnemolith.archivist_bait.hint: Drop it. An archivist will take the bait and freeze. Compose silence and player slips to make one.
item.mnemolith.archival_tablet.hint: Silence and a player, composed, become bait. A vein of this stone bleeds a little pressure and lets the lens read farther.
mnemolith.configuration.catalogEnabled.t: Whether a catalog fragment opens the discovery catalog.
mnemolith.configuration.discoveryHints.t: Whether the catalog and reel may show how many stable patterns are still unread. Unread patterns stay hidden.
mnemolith.configuration.lensOverlay.tool: Whether the chronicle lens draws the pressure pill above the hotbar.
mnemolith.configuration.overlayOpacity.t: Opacity, from 0.2 to 1.0, of the lens pressure pill. The band name stays readable.
mnemolith.configuration.showNumericPress: Whether the lens pill includes the numeric pressure beside the band name.
mnemolith.gui.catalog_empty: Extract an imprint. The catalog keeps only what you have learned.
mnemolith.gui.compose_fail: The slips refuse to hold together.
mnemolith.message.mute_first: Mute stone. This chunk will not take new imprints.
mnemolith.message.observatory_first: Chronicle observatory. The reel here still answers to the same formulas.
item.mnemolith.catalog_fragment.hint: Use to open the tags and patterns you have already learned.
item.mnemolith.field_guide.hint: Use to open illustrated notes on the memory loop.
mnemolith.guide.loop.title: The memory loop
mnemolith.guide.loop.body:
The world writes on its own. The server decides writes, pressure, extracts, and composes. The client draws the lens pill and this book. It does not replace the calculation.

A chunk holds at most 8 imprints by default: when it is full, the weakest one is dropped. The first copy of a tag adds its full pressure. Up to three further copies of the same tag add a quarter of that contribution, and at least 1. Copies after that do not count.

The needle takes the strongest imprint in the chunk into a slip and notes the tag for you. A formula on the reel is exactly a pair of tags. A third slip, or some other item, burns one item and counts as a failure. An empty reel spends nothing.

The catalog and the reel hints never name an unread formula. By default they only say how many patterns are still closed.
mnemolith.guide.sources.title: Where imprints come from
mnemolith.guide.sources.body:
A path is written about every 12 blocks. The first path contributes 1. It is a quiet tag.

Build and redstone are quiet too, contribution 2. A player who places or breaks a block writes two tags at once: build or redstone, and player. The player tag contributes 4, so the needle gives you the player slip first. Extract again for the build. The pause between those writes is 4 seconds by default. A mute stone itself is not a build write.

A fall is written from a distance of 4 blocks by default, contribution 10. A player's fall also adds the player tag. Death contributes 27. An explosion contributes 24. A death by fire also adds fire, contribution 8. If a player died, or a player struck the blow, a player tag is written beside it.

Silence, contribution 8, is written when a mute stone is placed. A death with no player within 32 blocks adds silence too. A witness inside those 32 blocks does not.

Quiet path, build, and redstone fade: after 6000 ticks by default, five minutes, one per pulse, while you stand in the chunk. Death, explosion, fall, fire, silence, and player stay until you extract them.
mnemolith.guide.bands.title: Pressure bands
mnemolith.guide.bands.body:
Pressure is the sum of imprint contributions and instability, capped by the soft ceiling. The ceiling is 100 by default. Band thresholds are multiplied by the storm scale, 1 by default, so the numbers below are the ones you play with.

Calm is below 20. Saturated starts at 20. Overloaded starts at 50. Fracture starts at 80.

The first time a chunk enters fracture, it is written to the log and asks for one moment replicant on the surface at the middle of the chunk. A fracture is also where recollection storms gather; see the storms page. Entering fracture again does not ask for another replicant by itself: the fracture flag is already set.

Instability is not an imprint. A failed compose adds it, 18 by default. While you stand in the chunk it cools by 1 every 200 ticks, ten seconds. An archival vein adds 1 per stratum by default and at most 6 per chunk. On its own that cannot change the band.

Overloaded and fracture chunks can condense a residual echo while you stand in them: 1 in 5 per 10 seconds, 1 in 2 in a fracture.
mnemolith.guide.mute.title: Stone and resonator
mnemolith.guide.mute.body:
Mute stone, in a column: ink sac, amethyst shard, cobblestone. When it is placed it writes silence first, and only then mutes. The radius is 0 by default: new imprints are refused in its own chunk. The setting can widen that radius across loaded chunks, no farther than two. Breaking the stone lifts the mute. The silence it already wrote stays until you extract it.

In a muted chunk an echo strider retreats and does not spawn naturally. A creature summoned by an egg or a command does not vanish because of the radius, but it still retreats from the mute.

Resonator trap, in a column: redstone, copper ingot, cobblestone. An archivist within 4 blocks is stunned for 80 ticks, four seconds. It checks the trap on its sensor, every 10 ticks by default, not every tick. The trap does not hold a strider or a replicant.

A residual echo in a muted chunk starves: it loses 1 strength every fester, writes nothing, and dissolves at 0.
mnemolith.guide.formulas.title: Formulas
mnemolith.guide.formulas.body:
Unrecorded is death and silence. 300 ticks, 15 seconds. While the effect is on you, a mob that selects you as a target drops that choice. It does not freeze and it does not go blind. Silence comes from placing a mute stone, or from a death with no player within 32 blocks. Death extracts before silence: take it first.

Fire trail is fire and build. 240 ticks, 12 seconds. For those same 12 seconds you get fire resistance, +0.04 speed, and every 10 ticks one snow layer underfoot melts. Fire arrives with a death by fire and leaves the needle after the death. A player writes build together with the player tag, and the needle gives up the player tag first.

Landing burst is fall and player. 400 ticks, 20 seconds. The next fall of at least 2 blocks deals 35% of its damage, once, and the effect ends. The fall imprint itself is written only from 4 blocks by default. A player's fall writes both tags; fall is stronger and comes out first.

Archivist bait is silence and player. It is an item, not an effect. It goes into your inventory, or onto the ground if there is no room. Drop it. Do not hold it.
mnemolith.guide.fails.title: A failed compose
mnemolith.guide.fails.body:
A wrong pair, an extra slip, or some other item destroys one item in the reel — the first slot that is not empty — and adds instability. The spike is 18 by default. Tags that were already in the slots are still noted for you.

A quiet failure is when pressure after the spike is still below 50, calm or saturated. No replicant is asked. On an empty chunk, 18 stays calm. At pressure 10 the result is 28, saturated, and still no replicant.

A loud failure starts at 32: 32 plus 18 makes 50, overloaded. From 62 the spike reaches fracture. The server asks for one moment replicant. It does not ask for a second while one is within 24 blocks or in that chunk's column, from the sky to the bottom of the world.

After a failure, stand in the chunk: instability cools by 1 every 10 seconds. Loud imprints do not fade from that.
mnemolith.guide.strider.title: Echo strider
mnemolith.guide.strider.body:
It walks a recent path. Health 24. A charge hits for 4, by default. Before the charge there is a telegraph of 45 ticks, a little over two seconds, and a low sound.

The charge starts if the chunk is overloaded or fractured, or if a player hit it. A hit is an invitation. In calm and saturated, without a hit, it only walks the path.

It spawns naturally in the overworld when pressure is at least 20. If the chunk already holds a path, the gate is 8 lower and starts at 12. The attempt chance is 35 out of 100. Natural spawn is refused in a muted chunk. An egg and /mnemolith spawn ignore the gate and the chance.

What to do. Place a mute stone and it retreats. Sneak with the lens in either hand within 8 blocks and it does the same. You do not need to use the lens. Do not hit it unless you are ready for the charge. If you hear the telegraph, step away or sneak with the lens. It drops a path slip.

What not to do. Do not stand on a walked trail in an overloaded chunk. Do not break the stone until you have left.

It trails a working echo like a recorded path, and charges it in overload. It does not notice a hushed echo.
mnemolith.guide.archivist.title: Archivist
mnemolith.guide.archivist.body:
The threat is theft, not the hit. The shove deals 2 damage, by default. It takes an interest in you within 16 blocks if your main hand holds a death or explosion slip: those tag weights are 9 and 8, and the interest gate is 8. Fall weighs 5 and does not start interest by itself.

Within 6 blocks, if it is already interested and 300 ticks have passed since the last theft, 15 seconds, it takes one slip. First from an open container, and everyone viewing that menu loses the same slip. Then from the inventory, if a slip is in a hand. In a menu and in an inventory it chooses the heavier tag, then runs. It also picks up a slip on the ground within 8 blocks, without choosing by weight.

Bait on the ground within 10 blocks: it walks over, eats one, and freezes for 100 ticks, five seconds. A resonator within 4 blocks stuns it for 4 seconds.

It spawns naturally at pressure of at least 50. Within two chunks of an observatory the gate is 14 lower and starts at 36. The attempt chance is 25 out of 100. An egg and a command ignore the gate.

What to do. Place a resonator by the chest before you open slips. Keep heavy slips out of your main hand. Throw bait off to the side, not at your feet.

What not to do. Do not open a chest of slips while it is nearby. Do not chase it: after a theft it is already running. Do not expect the stun to last: four or five seconds, and the chest is dangerous again.

Echoes. From a working echo it takes one stack (never a tool). If the echo carries a graft still worth a slip, it tears the graft out first. Everything it takes from an echo drops when it dies. It never notices a hushed echo.

Residual echoes. With empty hands it walks to an unread residue within 10 blocks and archives it. Kill it and the residual shard drops. A read, pinned residue is too bright for it.
mnemolith.guide.replicant.title: Moment replicant
mnemolith.guide.replicant.body:
It copies your last hit, jump, placed block, or item use. First a telegraph of 60 ticks, three seconds, then the replay. A hit up close deals 5 damage, by default. A jump throws it toward you. A placed block comes back as a replicated moment in front of you: a glassy block that fades after 10 seconds and drops nothing. It fills only air, and not when mob griefing is off. An item use is only a swing.

Where it comes from. The first fracture of a chunk asks for one on the surface at the middle of the chunk. A loud compose failure asks for one if none is in the chunk column or within 24 blocks. Natural spawn needs pressure of at least 80, chance 12 out of 100. An egg and a command ignore the gate. About one try in ten is a twin: if two players are nearby, its attention switches between them.

What to do. If you hear the telegraph, sneak and use the lens. Blindness for 4 seconds within 12 blocks clears the action it remembered. Compose in a quiet chunk, below 32, when the pair might be wrong.

What not to do. Do not push a chunk into fracture while you are standing in it. Do not build in a narrow corridor during the telegraph: the copy can block it for 10 seconds. Do not expect blindness to hold longer than four seconds.

It mimics a working echo's job for a while. It does not notice a hushed echo.
mnemolith.guide.echoes.title: Echoes at work
mnemolith.guide.echoes.body:
An echo slip records you, and the recording makes an echo. A lesson in the recording teaches it mining or building; pick the job in its screen (Shift + right-click).

Mobs. Hostile mobs (not creepers or neutral mobs) hunt a working echo. It never fights: the label says "Stop: attacked", it runs 8 blocks and goes back to work after 5 quiet seconds. An archivist steals one stack (not a tool, up to 8) from a working echo and always drops it when killed. A moment replicant mimics the job: it pulls up to three placed blocks back into the echo's inventory, or trips a miner. An echo strider trails the echo and charges it in overload.

Pressure. Every 20 blocks of work in one chunk leave a build imprint and a little instability; mute stone stops it. In overload the echo sometimes misfires: it skips a block or places a wrong one and fixes it itself later. In a fracture it stops. A second line over its head shows the band.

Farming. Till with a hoe, plant seeds or harvest ripe crops in a recording (2+ times) and the echo learns farming. The Farm button in its screen: it harvests ripe taught crops in range (up to 12), replants from its own seeds right away, sows empty farmland and carries the harvest to the chest, keeping up to 64 seeds. It never tramples farmland.

Getting around. An echo wades through shallow water (knee-deep, solid bottom), climbs ladders and vines, and opens wooden doors and fence gates, closing them behind it. It leaves iron doors and protected blocks alone.

Orders. Raise the lens (right-click) and aim at your echo: Z — stay (the job pauses), R — follow me (it stops if you get more than 48 blocks ahead), B — return to its point (walks back to the job and resumes it). Rebind the keys in Controls.

Upgrades, shapeless crafts, absorbed with right-click. Chorus slip: echo slip, unstable slip, archival tablet, amethyst — one more echo, up to three. Long take slip: echo slip, archivist husk, clock — recordings +10 seconds, twice. Sturdy body slip: echo slip, archival stratum, iron — health +10, twice.
mnemolith.guide.world.title: Places in the world
mnemolith.guide.world.body:
An archival vein, 8 attempts out of 100 by default, from Y -48 to 32, length 7. Stratum adds 1 pressure per block and at most 6 per chunk. On its own it does not change the band. With the lens in hand, reading that chunk reaches one chunk farther, and within 24 blocks the vein shimmers. An empty vein also lets the needle take an imprint from a loaded neighbor.

A mute pocket, 4 attempts out of 100 by default, from Y -32 to 48. The room is lined with mute stone, so new imprints are not written. It places into stone or air. About half of them have a chest. The chest holds one item: a tablet at weight 3, a needle at weight 1, or a silence slip at weight 2.

A chronicle observatory is placed with a spacing of 32 chunks and a separation of 12. The structureSpacing number in the config only records that. It does not move the buildings. Find one with /locate structure mnemolith:chronicle_observatory.

One roll in the chest is always a lens or a needle, equal weight. Two more rolls come from the teaching pool: tablet 6, mute stone 4, reel 2, silence slip 4, player slip 4, catalog fragment 1, this guide 2. An archivist nearby appears only once pressure reaches its gate, 36 by an observatory and 50 away from one, by default.

Every observatory also holds one old residual echo beside its reel, strength 5, which appears the first time you stand in that chunk. It does not fade in a calm chunk.

A Scar site is left wherever a recollection storm merged: a heart of cracked crystal ringed with scar glass. Storms never gather within a chunk of it, and once a day it seeds an old residue of strength 5. See the Scar page.
mnemolith.guide.players.title: Several players
mnemolith.guide.players.body:
One server decides writes, pressure, extracts, and composes for everyone. The band on the lens is the band the server calculated.

Discovery is personal. Your catalog does not show another player's tags, and their successful formula does not open the pattern for you. A slip you extracted stays with you, even if the imprint belonged to the shared chunk.

An archivist at an open chest takes one slip from the shared menu. Everyone viewing that menu loses it. From an inventory it takes from the player it is already interested in.

A twin replicant, about one try in ten, switches which of two nearby players it copies. An ordinary one watches the nearest player within 16 blocks.

Each client draws this book's pictures itself. A dedicated server does not load the guide screen. The book does not mute or heal a chunk.
mnemolith.guide.welcome.title: What Mnemolith is
mnemolith.guide.welcome.body:
A chunk remembers what happened in it. Walking, building, death, explosions, and falls leave imprints, and those imprints become pressure: calm, saturated, overloaded, fracture.

The lens reads that pressure. The needle lifts the strongest imprint into a slip. Two slips on a reel become a formula or a failure. The catalog shows only what you have learned.

Three creatures live on that memory: the echo strider, the archivist, and the moment replicant. The later pages say how to meet them and how to leave. This book does not change the chunk.

The dots along the bottom are chapters, and you can jump by them. The mouse wheel scrolls a long page. The arrows and buttons turn the page.

Your own recordings become echoes: bodies you can set to work, possess, and graft with the memories you extract. The echo pages come after the creatures.
mnemolith.guide.hour.title: The first hour
mnemolith.guide.hour.body:
The order below is survival advice, not a rule of the world. Start with what lets you see the loop.

1. Chronicle lens, in a column: amethyst shard, glass pane, copper ingot.
2. Extraction needle, in a column: amethyst shard, iron ingot, stick. It has 64 durability. By default a successful extract costs 2, then it rests 20 ticks — one second.
3. This guide: a book over an amethyst shard.
4. Composition reel, in a column: copper ingot, paper, crafting table.
5. Mute stone, in a column: ink sac, amethyst shard, cobblestone. Place it before the chunk gets loud.

Walk about 12 blocks and the chunk writes a path. Place or break an ordinary block for build. A block that emits a signal writes redstone. Those writes pause, 80 ticks by default, four seconds. Do not die in a camp you want to keep quiet.

An observatory is found with the ordinary command: /locate structure mnemolith:chronicle_observatory. Its chest always holds a lens or a needle.
mnemolith.guide.lens.title: Lens and reading
mnemolith.guide.lens.body:
Craft it in a column: amethyst shard, glass pane, copper ingot. Not a glass block and not a copper block — the pane and the ingot.

Hold the lens and a pressure pill appears above the hotbar. Without the lens there is no pill. Sneak and the pill adds the chunk state. Whether the number is shown is a client setting. The band on the pill matches the server.

Sneak and use the lens: replicants within 12 blocks are blinded for 80 ticks, four seconds, and forget the action they were about to copy. You do not need to hit a block.

An echo strider retreats if you are within 8 blocks, sneaking, with the lens in either hand. You do not need to use the item. Sneaking is enough.

On a chunk that holds archival stratum, a held lens reads one chunk farther: the usual radius of 2 becomes 3. Within 24 blocks of stratum the vein also shimmers. This book and the catalog do not read or write the chunk.

Residual echoes. A held lens makes residues easy to see. Raise it and keep it on one for 3 seconds, within 16 blocks, to read it: the tag is noted and the residue is pinned for 10 seconds.
mnemolith.guide.needle.title: Needle and slips
mnemolith.guide.needle.body:
Craft it in a column: amethyst shard, iron ingot, stick. Use the needle on a block.

It lifts the strongest imprint in that chunk, puts a slip in your inventory, and notes the tag. If the inventory is full, the slip drops. The needle has 64 durability. By default the strike costs 2, then it rests 20 ticks. An empty chunk with no vein says there is nothing to extract.

If the chunk has stratum and no imprints of its own left, the needle reaches into a loaded neighbor and takes the strongest imprint there. Without stratum it does not touch the neighbor.

Order matters. Death is louder than silence and fire. A player's fall is louder than the player tag. The player tag is louder than build and redstone. Take the strong one, then the weaker one that remains. Slips stack to 16, but the reel reads the tag in the slot, not the stack size: one slip goes into a slot.

On your own echo the needle unpicks its memory graft back into a slip, for the same durability and rest. A graft worn below half a slip crumbles instead.

On a residual echo the needle works only once the lens has read it: a pinned residue comes away as a residual shard, for 4 durability. On an unread one the needle slips and the residue lashes you.
mnemolith.guide.reel.title: The reel
mnemolith.guide.reel.body:
Craft it in a column: copper ingot, paper, crafting table. Place the block and open it.

A formula is exactly two tags. The reel has three slots, but a third tag matches no formula: the extra slip burns one item. Some other item in a slot is a failure too. An empty reel spends nothing and does not raise pressure.

A matching pair removes both slips, notes the formula for you, and gives an effect or an item. A wrong pair is the next page. Tags in the slots are noted on success and on failure.

Hints, on by default, only say how many patterns are still unread. Icons show what you have learned. The screen does not name a closed formula. Composition can be turned off in the config: the reel then refuses and does not spend slips.
mnemolith.guide.catalog.title: Catalog fragment
mnemolith.guide.catalog.body:
Craft it in a column: paper, amethyst shard, ink sac. Use the fragment and the catalog opens. If the catalog is turned off in the config, the fragment says it is closed.

A row appears only after the server has noted that tag or formula for you. Someone else's catalog does not show your notes, and your formula does not open the pattern for them. An unread formula is not named in the list. By default a hint says how many patterns are still closed.

The fragment does not write an imprint and does not lower pressure. In the observatory teaching pool its weight is 1. An archivist's drop is a catalog, paper, and ink, weights 2, 3, and 2, plus sometimes an archivist husk.
mnemolith.guide.reference.title: Quick sheet
mnemolith.guide.reference.body:
Crafts, all in a column. Lens: amethyst, glass pane, copper. Needle: amethyst, iron, stick. Guide: a book over amethyst. Reel: copper, paper, crafting table. Stone: ink, amethyst, cobblestone. Resonator: redstone, copper, cobblestone. Catalog: paper, amethyst, ink.

Bands by default: calm below 20, saturated from 20, overloaded from 50, fracture from 80, ceiling 100. A failure adds 18. A replicant is asked from overloaded onward, which means the pressure before the pair was already 32 or higher.

Formulas. Death + silence = Unrecorded, 15 seconds, mobs drop you as a target. Fire + build = fire trail, 12 seconds, fire resistance, +0.04 speed, snow melts. Fall + player = landing burst, 20 seconds, the next fall of at least 2 blocks deals 35% damage once. Silence + player = bait.

Defense. Strider: do not hit it; mute stone, or sneak with the lens within 8 blocks. Archivist: resonator within 4 blocks for 4 seconds, bait within 10 blocks for 5 seconds, heavy slips out of the main hand, do not open a chest beside it. Replicant: sneak and use the lens, blindness for 4 seconds within 12 blocks.

Observatory: /locate structure mnemolith:chronicle_observatory.

Echo crafts, shapeless. Echo slip: paper, amethyst, redstone, makes 2. Chorus slip: echo slip, unstable slip, archival tablet, amethyst. Long take slip: echo slip, archivist husk, clock. Sturdy body slip: echo slip, archival stratum, iron ingot.

Grafts, right-click your echo with a slip. Silence: hushed, 12 charges. Death: grave, 24. Fire: kindled, 32. Fall: plunging, 24. Explosion: volatile, 48. Two slips' worth at most. Needle unpicks; fracture rejects into the chunk; worn below half, it crumbles.

Residual echoes. Form: overloaded 1 in 5, fracture 1 in 2, per 10 seconds near you. Fester every 60 s: mute starves, matching echo drinks, calm fades, otherwise writes back (acts out in a fracture). Lens 3 s: read, pinned 10 s. Needle on a pinned one: residual shard, 4 durability. Shard on your echo: full graft from strength 4. Shard on a block: releases it.

Storms. Stand in a fracture: 2 in 100 per second, or free a shard there. Gather 10 s: mute stone in the centre or scar glass within a chunk contains it. Six waves every 10 s, up to 6 storm residues: mute starves, matching echo drinks, read holds, hushed echo swallows the act-out. 3+ left at the end: the Scar. Lens 3 s within 20 blocks: pinned 8 s, only then it can be hurt. Drops a scar fragment (scar-sets your echo: three slips of graft, fracture-proof) and a shard per temper. Site: storm-proof, an old residue once a day; break the heart to heal it.

Relay and vault. Relay thread: string, echo slip, copper, shapeless, makes 2; click two of your echoes within 16 blocks. Linked: auras at any distance, residues drunk for the partner, sneak + return key hops (5 s), your breaks and places mirrored within 6 blocks. Fracture under an end: noise. One end dies: the other takes 4 and a death memory. Archive vault: stratum and amethyst around a needle. Empty hand: draw on or off (loudest imprint of 3x3 chunks every 10 s, holds 12). 15% bleeds into its chunk; fracture spills half, explosion all; carried, it leaks one per 60 s. Needle takes one; sneak discharges all; idle feeds a grafted echo within 4; archivists raid it.

mnemolith.guide.recording.title: Echoes: record and possess
mnemolith.guide.recording.body:
Echo slip, shapeless: paper, amethyst shard, redstone. It makes 2. Use one and you are recorded for 25 seconds: movement, look, sneaking and sprinting, swings, broken and placed blocks, and levers, buttons and doors. Use it again to stop early. Under one second gives the slip back. The slip becomes an echo recording.

Use the recording within 48 blocks of where it started, in the same dimension, and an echo appears there: a translucent copy of you that replays the recording in the world, then stays as a helper. It starts with an empty inventory. Sneak and right-click it to give it tools and blocks. Right-click it with another recording to teach it again; its items stay. Only you can open, teach, graft or command your echo. You own one echo at first.

The replay is real. Blocks it breaks drop into its inventory, blocks it places come out of its inventory, and protection mods see you as the one acting. An echo takes no damage from falls, walls or water, heals slowly and does not despawn. If it dies, its items drop, the chunk gets 24 instability and a death imprint.

The lens. Hold right-click with the chronicle lens: the screen turns rose and every echo shows through walls. Aim at your own echo within 32 blocks and press attack to possess it. Your body stays behind as a shell, and you walk in the echo with its items and health. V brings you back. If the shell is killed, you die there with your real items. If the body dies, you wake in the shell and the body's items drop where it fell. Logging out, changing dimension or a server stop always brings you back first.

A recording that breaks two or more blocks teaches mining. One that places blocks teaches building. One that tills, plants or harvests twice teaches farming. The next page is about those jobs.
mnemolith.guide.grafts.title: Memory grafts
mnemolith.guide.grafts.body:
An echo is made of your memory. You can give it another one. Right-click your own echo with an imprint slip and the slip is grafted: the echo takes a temper, its body changes color, and motes of that color drift off it. One slip gives a graft its charges. Another slip of the same tag feeds the graft, up to two slips' worth. A slip of another tag replaces it. The echo screen and the lens label show the temper and the charges left.

Only memories of something happening to a body take: silence, death, fire, fall and explosion. Path, build, redstone and player slips only remember who was there, and an echo already is that.

Hushed (silence, 12 charges). Its work, and the work of your echoes within 8 blocks, writes no imprints and no instability. Each swallowed imprint costs 1. Hostile mobs, archivists, striders and replicants do not notice it. It digs and places about a third slower.

Grave (death, 24). A decoy. Hostile mobs turn to it, even away from you, even while it stands idle. It does not run: each hit costs 1, and it still takes the damage.

Kindled (fire, 32). Fireproof. It may mine next to lava, never next to water. Ore that it, or your echoes within 8 blocks, mine comes out smelted: iron ore gives iron ingots. Each smelted ore costs 1. Its work imprints are fire, not build.

Plunging (fall, 24). It walks off drops of up to 12 blocks and digs out the floor under itself over such a drop. Each long drop or floor dig costs 1.

Volatile (explosion, 48). It digs almost twice as fast; each dug block costs 1. Its work imprints are explosions, so the chunk climbs fast. When its body dies it bursts: the blast breaks no blocks but hurts everything near it, your echoes and you included.

Possession. Possess a grafted echo and you carry its temper. Hushed gives Unrecorded, grave Resistance, kindled Fire Resistance (paid only while you burn), volatile Haste II: 1 charge per 10 seconds. A plunging body takes no fall damage; each hard landing costs 1. A volatile body that dies while you are in it vents its explosion into the chunk without a blast.

Where a graft goes. The extraction needle on your echo unpicks the graft back into its slip, for 2 durability. A fracture under the echo rejects the graft back into the chunk as its imprint. A dying echo leaves its graft in the chunk too. A muted chunk refuses it, and it drops as a slip. A graft worn below half a slip's charges crumbles instead. An archivist robbing a working echo tears the graft out first and drops it as a slip when killed.

Tips. Make slips on purpose: a fall of 4 blocks writes fall, TNT writes explosion, a mute stone writes silence, a mob burnt to death writes death and fire. A kindled miner's fire imprints can be extracted to feed it again, if the chunk holds. A hushed echo beside a volatile miner keeps the fast crew quiet until the hush runs out.

In an overloaded or fractured chunk a released graft does not go back as an imprint: it condenses into a residual echo. A residual shard grafts at up to two slips' worth at once. See the residual echoes page.

mnemolith.guide.residues.title: Residual echoes
mnemolith.guide.residues.body:
An overloaded chunk cannot hold everything. About every 10 seconds while you stand in one, there is a 1 in 5 chance (1 in 2 in a fracture) that its loudest memory of a body, silence, death, fire, fall or explosion, condenses out of it into a residual echo: a faint fragment of a figure in that memory's color, drifting inside the chunk. The imprint is gone from the chunk, so pressure drops. Path, build, redstone and player never condense. One residue per chunk, at most 3 within 48 blocks.

What it does if you leave it. Every 60 seconds it festers. In a loud chunk it writes its memory back, so the pressure you lost climbs again. In a fracture it also acts it out: death raises a zombie (at most 2 near it), fire lights a fire, an explosion goes off small, fall lifts players within 8, silence brings darkness. Fire and blasts respect mobGriefing. Walk within 3 blocks of an unread one (1.5 sneaking) and it lashes: fire sets you alight, fall throws you up, death hurts and withers, an explosion bursts at your feet, silence blinds. Every 5 seconds at most. It cannot be hurt.

Observe. Raise the lens (hold right-click) and keep it on the residue for 3 seconds, within 16 blocks. It is read: its tag is noted for you, and for 10 seconds it is pinned, bright, slow and harmless. The lens label shows what it is and how far the reading is.

Capture. The extraction needle on a pinned residue takes it as a residual shard, for twice the needle's usual wear (4). On an unread one the needle slips and the residue lashes you.

Exploit. A festering residue in a loud chunk is a slip farm: extract what it writes. An echo grafted with the same temper within 6 blocks drinks it instead: half a slip of charges per fester, and the residue weakens. Possess an echo and right-click a residue with an empty hand: the body takes its lash, then wears it as a graft, full from strength 4.

Residual shard. It cannot be crafted. It comes from the needle on a read residue, or from an archivist: one with empty hands walks to an unread residue within 10 blocks, archives it and runs; kill it and the shard drops. Right-click your echo with a shard: it grafts at full two slips' worth from strength 4 (strength 3 gives one and a half, 2 gives one). Use it on a block to set the residue free there with its strength, to feed an echo station or to farm slips where you want.

Let it be, or starve it. A mute stone in its chunk starves it: it loses 1 strength per fester and writes nothing. In a calm chunk it fades by 1 per fester. At 0 it dissolves. A graft released in an overloaded chunk (a fracture rejecting it, a dying echo) condenses into a residue instead of an imprint.

Old residues. Every chronicle observatory holds one: strength 5, beside the reel, the first time you stand in that chunk. An old residue does not fade in a calm chunk. It is the easiest full graft in the world, if you read it before the archivists find it.
item.mnemolith.scar_fragment.hint: Right-click your echo: scar-sets it for good. Its graft holds three slips' worth, and a fracture no longer rejects the graft or stops its work. One per echo.

mnemolith.scar.read: Read: the Scar is pinned for %s seconds. Strike now.

mnemolith.guide.storms.title: Recollection storms
mnemolith.guide.storms.body:
A fracture remembers too much at once. Once a second, for each player standing in a fractured chunk, there is a 2 in 100 chance (stormAttemptChance) that a recollection storm starts gathering there. Freeing a residual shard on a block in a fractured chunk calls one at once, and the freed residue is the storm's first. One storm per dimension by default (maxStormsPerDimension).

Gathering, 10 seconds. A bar appears for everyone within 48 blocks, the sky darkens, the edge of the storm's area, the 3x3 chunks around its centre, flickers. Prepare or leave. A mute stone in the centre chunk, or scar glass within one chunk of it, contains the storm: it ends before it breaks.

Raging: six waves, one every 10 seconds. Each wave condenses the loudest memories of a body (silence, death, fire, fall, explosion) out of the area into storm residues, up to 6 at once; a muted chunk gives none. Then every storm residue takes its turn. In a muted chunk it starves and loses 1 strength. An echo grafted with its temper within 6 blocks drinks it: half a slip of charges, and it weakens. A read (pinned) one holds still. Every other one acts its memory out: death raises a zombie (at most 2 near it), fire lights a fire, an explosion goes off small, fall lifts players within 8, silence brings darkness. Fire and blasts respect mobGriefing. A hushed echo, anyone's, within 8 blocks swallows an act-out for one charge. A muted centre chunk chokes the storm: each wave there counts twice. Storm residues do not fester or write back, but they still lash whoever walks close, and what they act out (a dead zombie, a blast) leaves new memories for the next wave.

How it ends. Nothing standing and nothing left to condense: it is spent. After the last wave, fewer than 3 standing: it passes, and they stay as ordinary residues. Three or more: they merge into the Scar (next page). If nobody is near, the storm waits, frozen, until its centre loads again.

Choices. Drain the area first: extract or starve its loud memories, and the storm has nothing to feed on. Read storm residues and take them with the needle: each capture is a shard, and one fewer to merge. Bring grafted echoes to drink them. Contain it with a mute stone while it gathers. Or let it merge, if you want what the Scar drops.
mnemolith.guide.scar.title: The Scar
mnemolith.guide.scar.body:
When three or more storm residues outlast the waves, they merge. The storm's centre becomes a Scar site, and the Scar rises over it (not on peaceful).

The Scar. A great cracked residue in the colors of what merged into it, 60 health plus 20 per merged residue (120 for three, at most 180). It cannot be hurt until it is read: keep the raised lens on it for 3 seconds within 20 blocks, and for 8 seconds it is pinned, slow, silent and open to your blows. Then it cannot be read again for 5 seconds. It stays within 20 blocks of its heart and heals when nobody is within 32.

Its recall. Every 3 seconds, after a one-second charge you can hear, it plays one of its memories, in turn: every player within 10 blocks takes that residue's lash, and the memory is acted out once at the first of them. A grave-grafted echo within 16 blocks draws the whole recall onto itself, one charge each. A hushed echo within 8 blocks swallows the act-out, one charge. A mute stone in its chunk halves its recalls and keeps it from writing its memories into the chunk.

What it drops. A scar fragment (two if five or more residues merged), a residual shard of strength 4 for each temper that merged, and experience. A scar fragment on your own echo scar-sets it for good: its graft holds three slips' worth instead of two, and a fracture neither rejects the graft nor stops its work. One per echo.

The site. With mobGriefing on, the Scar grows its heart at the centre and a ring of scar glass around it, only into air or plants, never over your blocks. No storm gathers within one chunk of a site. Once per in-game day, when you stand in its chunk, the site seeds one old residue of strength 5, of a temper that merged there, by the heart, unless a mute stone silences the chunk or a residue is already there: a full graft every day for whoever reads it first. Break the heart (it drops nothing) and the site heals: no more seeding, and storms may come back.

Scar glass. Mine it with a pickaxe; it drops itself. Placed anywhere, it is a ward: no storm gathers within one chunk of it, and unlike a mute stone it still lets imprints be written. Guard your slip farm with it.
mnemolith.configuration.relayEnabled.too: Whether relay threads can link echoes, and whether existing links do anything (aura conduit, residue relay, hop, mirror, death shock). Links stay saved while this is off.
mnemolith.configuration.relayLinkRange.t: Blocks within which the second echo must stand from the first when you tie the link. Once tied, the link works at any distance in the same dimension while both ends are loaded.
mnemolith.configuration.relayHopCooldown: Seconds between two relay hops (sneak and press the return key while possessing a linked echo). 0 means no wait.
mnemolith.configuration.relayMirror.tool: Whether a linked echo repeats the blocks you break and place while you possess its partner, at the same offset from its own feet (within 6 blocks, with its own tools and blocks).
mnemolith.configuration.vaultsEnabled.to: Whether archive vaults draw, bleed pressure, feed echoes, get raided and leak when carried. Stored imprints are kept while this is off.
mnemolith.configuration.vaultDrawSeconds: Seconds between two draws of a drawing vault (the loudest imprint from its chunk and the eight around it), and between two echo feeds and rupture checks of an idle one.
mnemolith.configuration.vaultBleed.toolt: Share of the stored imprints' pressure that bleeds into the vault's own chunk (0.15: twelve deaths add about 49). A vault is never free: it moves pressure, it does not delete it.
mnemolith.configuration.vaultLeakSeconds: Seconds between two leaks of a filled vault carried in a player's inventory: one of its imprints, at random, is written where the carrier stands. 0 turns leaking off.
item.mnemolith.relay_thread.hint: Right-click one of your echoes, then another within 16 blocks: they are linked. Sneak-click cuts a link. Linked echoes share hush and kindle auras at any distance, drink residues for each other, and you can hop between them while possessing (sneak + return key).
item.mnemolith.relay_thread.source: Crafted, shapeless: string, echo slip, copper ingot, makes 2. One thread is used per link.
item.mnemolith.relay_thread.first: First end tied. Now click the second echo.
block.mnemolith.archive_vault.hint: Right-click to start or stop drawing: it pulls the loudest imprint out of the nearby chunks every 10 s, up to 12. What it holds bleeds pressure into its own chunk; a fracture there or an explosion spills it. Needle: take one out as a slip. Sneak-click: discharge all.
block.mnemolith.archive_vault.source: Crafted, shaped: stratum, amethyst, stratum / amethyst, extraction needle, amethyst / stratum, amethyst, stratum. Mine with a pickaxe: it keeps what it holds, but leaks while carried.

mnemolith.relay.shock: A linked echo died: the thread snapped and its partner took the shock.

mnemolith.relay.hop.not_possessing: You are not in an echo.

mnemolith.relay.hop.noisy: A fracture fills the thread with noise: you cannot hop.

mnemolith.guide.relay.title: The echo relay
mnemolith.guide.relay.body:
A relay thread ties two of your echoes into one pair. Right-click the first with the thread, then the second within 16 blocks (relayLinkRange); one thread is used. Sneak-click either end with a thread to cut the link. An echo has one link at a time; tying a new one cuts the old. Right-click an echo you own to see its relay line: linked and how far, noise, or the other end not loaded.

What the thread carries, at any distance in the same dimension while both ends are loaded:

Auras. Each end stands inside its partner's hush and kindle aura. A hushed echo at home swallows the work imprints of its partner mining far away (one charge each); a kindled one smelts its ore. The graft's owner pays.

Residues. An echo next to a residue drinks it for its partner when the partner carries that temper: half a slip of charges goes down the thread.

You. While possessing one end, sneak and press the return key: you hop into the other end. The body you leave stands back up as an echo with its items; your shell and real self stay where they are. Cooldown 5 seconds (relayHopCooldownSeconds).

Your hands. While you possess one end, every block you break or place is repeated by the other end at the same offset from its feet, with its own tools and blocks: dig a stair here, and a stair is dug there. It skips blocks with contents, targets more than 6 blocks from it, and a partner that is replaying or working a job.

Risks. A fracture under either end turns the thread to noise: nothing passes, and no hop. When one end dies, even a body you possess, the thread snaps: the other end takes 4 damage and a death memory is written under it.

Craft: string, echo slip, copper ingot, shapeless, makes 2.
mnemolith.guide.vault.title: The archive vault
mnemolith.guide.vault.body:
An archive vault banks memory. Pressure stops being only a threat: you can store it, carry it and spend it, and each of those has a price.

Bank. Right-click with an empty hand: the vault starts drawing and glows. Every 10 seconds (vaultDrawSeconds) it pulls the loudest imprint out of its chunk and the eight around it, up to 12 (vaultCapacity). Muted chunks are skipped. Right-click again to stop. Right-click shows how full it is and its load.

Bleed. Nothing is deleted. 15% of what it holds (vaultBleed) weighs on the vault's own chunk as pressure: twelve deaths add about 49. Put it somewhere you can afford to be loud, or far from your base.

Rupture. If the vault's chunk reaches fracture, at its next tick half of what it holds, the loudest first, spills back into that chunk, and again every tick while the fracture lasts. An explosion spills everything. A mute stone in the chunk swallows a spill: those imprints are lost.

Move. Mine it with a pickaxe: it keeps its contents on the item. While you carry a filled vault, every 60 seconds (vaultLeakSeconds) one imprint leaks where you stand.

Spend. The extraction needle takes the loudest one out as a slip, for formulas and grafts. Sneak-click with an empty hand discharges all of it into its chunk at once (a mute stone refuses): a way to feed a storm or build a fracture on purpose. An idle vault feeds one grafted echo within 4 blocks: an imprint of its temper becomes half a slip of charges.

Thieves. An archivist with free hands within 10 blocks goes for a filled vault and takes its loudest imprint; kill it to get the slip back.

Craft: archival stratum, amethyst, stratum / amethyst, extraction needle, amethyst / stratum, amethyst, stratum. Stratum is mined from archival veins.
